title: IBPS SO IT Mains – Day 2: Computer Networks
answer_format: answer is the option letter a–e mapping to options[0]–options[4]

questions.question: Which PDU corresponds to the Transport layer of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: Transport layer PDU is a Segment (TCP). Sequence: Bit (L1), Frame (L2), Packet (L3), Segment (L4).

questions.question: At which OSI layer does a repeater operate?
questions.explanation: A repeater only regenerates the signal, so it works at the Physical layer (L1).

questions.question: Which device separates broadcast domains?
questions.explanation: Routers stop broadcasts. A switch separates only collision domains; a hub separates nothing.

questions.question: According to IEEE 802.3, what is the maximum length of a single 100Base-TX segment?
questions.explanation: All twisted-pair (-T / -TX) Ethernet standards have a 100 m limit.

questions.question: HDLC is an example of a:
questions.explanation: HDLC is bit-oriented: flag 01111110 with bit stuffing. PPP is byte-oriented.

questions.question: Which type of VLAN port carries traffic for multiple VLANs over a single link?
questions.explanation: A trunk port carries many VLANs (802.1Q tags). An access port carries one VLAN.

questions.question: A walkie-talkie is an example of which transmission mode?
questions.explanation: Half duplex: both directions, but one at a time.

questions.question: CSMA/CA is mainly used in:
questions.explanation: CSMA/CA (Avoidance) is used over the Air (Wi-Fi). CSMA/CD (Detection) is used on Cable (Ethernet).

questions.question: Which error detection method does Ethernet use?
questions.explanation: Ethernet's FCS field uses CRC-32. Checksums are used by IP, TCP and UDP.

questions.question: Which switch feature copies traffic from one port to another so that it can be inspected by a packet analyzer?
questions.explanation: Port mirroring (SPAN) copies a port's traffic to a monitoring port.

questions.question: Which device gives each port its own collision domain but keeps all ports in a single broadcast domain?
questions.explanation: A switch separates collision domains per port, but all ports remain in one broadcast domain.

questions.question: What is the maximum segment length for twisted-pair Ethernet standards such as 10Base-T and 1000Base-T?
questions.explanation: Twisted-pair Ethernet is limited to 100 m. 185 m is 10Base2 (thin coax), 500 m is 10Base5 (thick coax).

questions.question: Which of the following is a byte-oriented protocol?
questions.explanation: PPP is byte-oriented and uses byte stuffing. HDLC and SDLC are bit-oriented.

questions.question: Which IEEE standard is used to tag frames when multiple VLANs travel over a trunk link?
questions.explanation: 802.1Q adds a 4-byte VLAN tag. 802.1D is STP, 802.11 Wi-Fi, 802.15 Bluetooth.

questions.question: Wired Ethernet networks use which media access method?
questions.explanation: Wired Ethernet uses CSMA/CD (Collision Detection).

questions.question: The Frame Check Sequence (FCS) field in an Ethernet frame uses:
questions.explanation: The FCS is a CRC-32 value. A TCP checksum belongs to the Transport layer, not the Ethernet frame.

questions.question: A network administrator wants an IDS to see all the traffic passing through a specific switch port. Which feature should they configure?
questions.explanation: Port mirroring (SPAN) copies the port's traffic to the IDS / analyzer port.

questions.question: How many links are needed to fully connect 6 devices in a mesh topology?
What is the size of a MAC address?
questions.explanation: A MAC address is 48 bits (12 hex digits). The first 24 bits are the OUI.

questions.question: When an error occurs in Go-Back-N ARQ, which frames are retransmitted?
options: Only the frames after the lost one
The lost frame and all frames sent after it
questions.explanation: Go-Back-N's receiver accepts only in-order frames, so the sender resends the lost frame and everything after it.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for routing?
questions.explanation: Routing (choosing paths using IP addresses) is the Network layer's job.

questions.question: In HDLC bit stuffing, the sender:
options: Inserts an escape byte before the flag
Adds a parity bit after every byte
questions.explanation: After five 1s a 0 is inserted, so the flag 01111110 never appears inside data.

questions.question: Using a Hamming code, how many redundant bits are needed to protect 4 data bits?
questions.explanation: Smallest r with 2^r >= m + r + 1: 2^3 = 8 >= 4 + 3 + 1 = 8, so r = 3.

questions.question: Which protocol prevents loops in a network of interconnected switches?
questions.explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol blocks redundant ports to keep the topology loop-free.

questions.question: In Selective Repeat ARQ, which frames are retransmitted after an error?
options: The lost frame and all frames sent after it
Only the lost or damaged frame
Only the frames sent before the lost one
questions.explanation: Selective Repeat buffers out-of-order frames and resends only the lost one.

questions.question: What is the maximum efficiency of Slotted ALOHA?
questions.explanation: Slotted ALOHA = 36.8%; Pure ALOHA = 18.4%.

questions.question: Which of the following is the Ethernet broadcast MAC address?
questions.explanation: All 1s (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF) is the MAC broadcast. 255.255.255.255 is an IP broadcast, not a MAC.

questions.question: Which technology combines several physical links between two switches into one logical link, to increase bandwidth and provide redundancy?
questions.explanation: Link aggregation (LACP, 802.3ad) bundles physical links into one logical link.

questions.question: Which connector is commonly used with coaxial cable?
questions.explanation: Coax uses BNC. RJ45 is twisted-pair Ethernet, RJ11 is telephone, LC is fiber.

questions.question: Match each OSI layer with its function. Layers: 1. Network, 2. Transport, 3. Data Link, 4. Physical. Functions: (a) Access control, (b) Channel transmission, (c) Routing, (d) Segmentation and reassembly.
questions.explanation: Network = Routing, Transport = Segmentation and reassembly, Data Link = Access control, Physical = Channel transmission.

questions.question: What is the total number of networks available in IPv4 Class C?
questions.explanation: Class C has 24 network bits; the first 3 are fixed (110), leaving 21 free bits: 2²¹.

questions.question: Which of the following is a private IP address?
questions.explanation: Private Class B is 172.16 to 172.31, so 172.20.5.1 is private. 172.32 and 192.169 are public.

questions.question: A Class B network (/16) must be divided into at least 500 subnets. Which subnet mask should be used?
How many usable hosts are there in each subnet of 192.168.1.0/27?
What is the network address of 10.1.70.5/20?
questions.explanation: /20 gives block 16 in the 3rd octet. 70 lies in 64 to 79, so the network is 10.1.64.0.

questions.question: When a router decrements a packet's TTL to 0, what does it do?
options: Forwards the packet with TTL reset to 64
Discards the packet and sends an ICMP Time Exceeded message to the source
Returns the packet to the previous router
Increases the TTL and forwards the packet
questions.explanation: TTL 0 means the packet is dropped and ICMP Time Exceeded is sent back. This prevents infinite loops.

questions.question: A router receives an IP packet that is larger than the MTU of the outgoing link, and the DF bit is set. What does the router do?
options: Fragments the packet and forwards it
Drops the packet and sends an ICMP 'Fragmentation Needed' message
questions.explanation: DF = Don't Fragment, so the router can't split it. It drops the packet and reports 'Fragmentation Needed'.

questions.question: Which of the following is an IPv6 link-local address?
questions.explanation: Link-local addresses start with FE80. FF = multicast, ::1 = loopback, 2001 = global, FD = unique local.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: IPv6 has no broadcast; multicast does that job.

questions.question: A packet starts with a hop limit of 64 and passes through 5 routers before reaching its destination. What is its hop limit on arrival?
questions.explanation: Each router decrements by 1: 64 - 5 = 59.

questions.question: In IPv4 Class B, the first octet falls in which range?
A /16 network is subnetted using a /22 mask. How many subnets are created?
questions.explanation: Bits borrowed = 22 - 16 = 6, so 2^6 = 64 subnets.

questions.question: How many usable hosts does each subnet have with mask 255.255.255.240?
questions.explanation: Block size = 256 - 240 = 16, so usable hosts = 16 - 2 = 14.

questions.question: What is the broadcast address of the subnet containing 192.168.5.77/28?
questions.explanation: /28 block = 16. 77 lies in 64 to 79, so the broadcast is .79.

questions.question: A Windows PC shows the IP address 169.254.10.5. What does this most likely mean?
options: It has a static public IP
It is on a Class D multicast network
It is using the loopback interface
It has been assigned an IPv6 address
It failed to get an address from a DHCP server and assigned itself an APIPA address
questions.explanation: 169.254.x.x is APIPA, self-assigned when DHCP fails.

questions.question: A 3000-byte IPv4 packet (20-byte header + 2980 bytes of data) must cross a link with an MTU of 1500 bytes. How many fragments are created?
questions.explanation: Max data per fragment = 1480. 2980 = 1480 + 1480 + 20, so 3 fragments.

questions.question: In the IPv4 header, the Fragment Offset field is measured in units of:
questions.explanation: Fragment offset is in 8-byte units, which is why fragment data sizes must be multiples of 8.

questions.question: What value in the IPv4 Protocol field indicates that the payload is TCP?
questions.explanation: 1 = ICMP, 6 = TCP, 17 = UDP.

questions.question: Which is the correct shortened form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329?
questions.explanation: Drop leading zeros in each group and replace one run of zero groups with :: (only once).

questions.question: What is the size of the IPv6 base header?
questions.explanation: IPv6 base header is a fixed 40 bytes. IPv4 header is 20 to 60 bytes.

questions.question: Which mechanism translates private internal IP addresses into public IP addresses, letting LAN devices communicate externally while concealing their internal addresses?
questions.explanation: NAT translates private to public addresses and hides internal addressing.

questions.question: What is the primary function of ARP in an IPv4 local network?
options: To resolve domain names into IP addresses
To find the MAC address that corresponds to an IP address
questions.explanation: ARP resolves IP to MAC. DHCP assigns IPs; DNS resolves names.

questions.question: What is the correct order of messages in the DHCP process?
questions.explanation: DORA: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

questions.question: The traceroute command discovers the path to a host by relying on:
options: Increasing TTL values and ICMP Time Exceeded messages
questions.explanation: Traceroute sends packets with TTL 1, 2, 3... and each router that drops one reveals itself via ICMP Time Exceeded.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of sequence numbers in TCP?
options: To count the routers in a path
To ensure data is delivered in the correct order
To identify the receiver's port number
To detect congestion in the network
questions.explanation: Sequence numbers let TCP deliver data in order and detect lost or duplicate segments.

questions.question: Which of the following normally uses UDP?
questions.explanation: DNS queries use UDP 53. HTTP, FTP, SMTP and SSH use TCP.

questions.question: In the TCP 3-way handshake, which message does the server send in the second step?
questions.explanation: Handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.

questions.question: A 1000-byte packet is sent on a 4 Mbps link. What is the transmission delay?

A 4000-bit packet travels through 3 intermediate routers using store-and-forward switching. Every link has a rate of 2 Mbps. Ignoring propagation, queuing and processing delays, what is the total delay?
questions.explanation: Per link 4000 / 2,000,000 = 2 ms. Links = N + 1 = 4, so 8 ms.

questions.question: Which TCP mechanism prevents a fast sender from overflowing the receiver's buffer?
questions.explanation: Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects the network.

questions.question: What is the maximum hop count allowed by RIP?
questions.explanation: RIP allows up to 15 hops; 16 means unreachable.

questions.question: Which routing protocol is used to exchange routes between autonomous systems on the internet?
questions.explanation: BGP is the internet's routing protocol between autonomous systems (TCP 179).

questions.question: The ping command uses which protocol?
questions.explanation: Ping sends ICMP Echo Request and waits for Echo Reply.

questions.question: A link is 3000 km long and the signal speed is 2 × 10⁸ m/s. What is the propagation delay?
DHCP uses which transport protocol and ports?
questions.explanation: DHCP: UDP 67 (server) and 68 (client).

questions.question: Which type of NAT lets many private devices share a single public IP address by using port numbers to tell them apart?
questions.explanation: PAT (NAT overload) maps many private hosts to one public IP using ports. Home routers use this.

questions.question: What is the size of the UDP header?
questions.explanation: UDP header = 8 bytes. TCP header = 20 to 60 bytes.

questions.question: If the bandwidth of a link is doubled, which delay changes?
questions.explanation: Transmission = L/R depends on bandwidth. Propagation = d/s does not.

questions.question: A 2000-byte packet is sent on an 8 Mbps link with a propagation delay of 5 ms. What is the total delay over this single link?
questions.explanation: Transmission = 16000 / 8,000,000 = 2 ms. Total = 2 + 5 = 7 ms.

questions.question: Which protocol resolves a MAC address to an IP address?
questions.explanation: RARP = Reverse ARP (MAC to IP). ARP does IP to MAC.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: UDP guarantees delivery of every datagram
UDP has less overhead than TCP
questions.explanation: UDP is unreliable; it does not guarantee delivery.

questions.question: TCP congestion control is mainly designed to protect:
questions.explanation: Congestion control protects the network. Flow control protects the receiver.

questions.question: In what order does a DNS resolver contact servers to translate a domain name into an IP address?
options: TLD server → Root server → Authoritative server
Authoritative server → TLD server → Root server
Root server → TLD server → Authoritative server
TLD server → Authoritative server → Root server
Root server → Authoritative server → TLD server
questions.explanation: Root, then TLD (.com), then the authoritative server, which returns the IP.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code means Internal Server Error?
questions.explanation: 500 = Internal Server Error. 5xx = server errors.

questions.question: How do SMTP and POP3 differ?
options: SMTP retrieves emails, while POP3 sends them
SMTP secures messages, while POP3 stores them permanently
SMTP manages file transfers, while POP3 manages attachments
Both protocols perform the same function
SMTP sends emails, while POP3 downloads them
questions.explanation: SMTP sends/pushes mail; POP3 downloads mail to a device.

questions.question: What is the default port used by RDP?
questions.explanation: RDP = 3389. 1433 = SQL Server, 3306 = MySQL, 22 = SSH.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a feature of IMAP?
options: Emails are automatically deleted from the server after download
Users can manage server-side mailbox properties such as read status and folders
Emails can be transferred only within a local network
Emails can be accessed only offline
questions.explanation: IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs folders and read status across devices.

questions.question: Which DNS record identifies the mail server for a domain?
questions.explanation: MX = Mail Exchanger. A = IPv4, AAAA = IPv6, CNAME = alias, PTR = reverse lookup.

questions.question: Which transport layer protocol does SMTP use?
questions.explanation: SMTP runs over TCP (port 25).

questions.question: Which port does FTP use for its control connection?
questions.explanation: FTP: 21 = control, 20 = data.

questions.question: What does the HTTP status code 404 mean?
questions.explanation: 404 = Not Found. 401 = Unauthorized, 403 = Forbidden, 502 = Bad Gateway, 301 = Moved Permanently.

questions.question: In email handling, what is the role of a user agent?
options: It transfers emails between mail servers
It provides the interface for users to compose, send and read emails
It permanently stores emails on the server
questions.explanation: The user agent is the email app (Outlook, Gmail app). Mail servers (MTAs) transfer mail between servers.

questions.question: What is the default port number for Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP)?
Which protocol uses port 22?
questions.explanation: 22 = SSH (secure, lower number); 23 = Telnet.

questions.question: You can't connect to a website, even though your internet connection is working. What is the most likely reason?
options: The browser cache hasn't been cleared
The DNS server is down or misconfigured
The website's IP address changed recently
The monitor's resolution is too low
questions.explanation: If the connection works but names don't resolve, DNS is the most likely problem.

questions.question: By default, what happens to emails on the server when they are retrieved using POP3?
options: They are synchronised across all devices
They are moved into server-side folders
They are forwarded to another server
They are encrypted on the server
They are downloaded to the device and deleted from the server
questions.explanation: POP3 downloads and (by default) deletes from the server. IMAP keeps mail on the server.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols is NOT part of the HTTP/HTTPS web communication protocol family?
questions.explanation: FTP is a separate file transfer protocol. WebDAV is an extension of HTTP.

questions.question: Which practice is used to hide the IP addresses of backend servers from clients?
questions.explanation: A reverse proxy sits in front of servers and hides their IPs. A forward proxy acts for clients.

questions.question: A logged-in user tries to open an admin page they don't have permission to view. Which HTTP status code is returned?
questions.explanation: 403 Forbidden: identity is known but access is not allowed. 401 means not authenticated.

questions.question: SNMP is primarily used for:
questions.explanation: SNMP = Simple Network Management Protocol (UDP 161/162).

questions.question: How does a CDN improve website performance?
options: By assigning IP addresses to users
By serving content from edge servers close to the user
questions.explanation: CDNs cache content on edge servers near users, reducing latency.

questions.question: Why is Telnet considered insecure compared with SSH?
options: It sends data, including passwords, in plaintext
questions.explanation: Telnet (TCP 23) sends everything in plaintext. SSH encrypts.

questions.question: Port 23 is used by:
questions.explanation: 23 = Telnet; 22 = SSH.

questions.question: HTTPS uses port:
questions.explanation: HTTPS = 443; HTTP = 80.

questions.question: Port 110 is used by:
IMAP uses port:
questions.explanation: IMAP = 143 (993 when secured).

questions.question: Port 53 is used by:
questions.explanation: 53 = DNS.

questions.question: SNMP uses port:
questions.explanation: SNMP = 161 (162 for traps). 123 = NTP, 389 = LDAP, 69 = TFTP.

questions.question: Port 25 is used by:
questions.explanation: 25 = SMTP.

questions.question: Microsoft SQL Server uses port:
questions.explanation: SQL Server = 1433; MySQL = 3306; RDP = 3389.

questions.question: The FTP data connection uses port:
questions.explanation: FTP data = 20; FTP control = 21.

questions.question: Port 3306 is used by:
questions.explanation: 3306 = MySQL.

questions.question: Which PDU corresponds to the Network layer?
questions.explanation: Network layer PDU = Packet.

questions.question: In IPv4 Class C, the first octet falls in which range?
questions.explanation: Class C = 192 to 223.

questions.question: Which of the following is a private IP address?
questions.explanation: 192.168.x.x is private. 172.15 and 172.32 fall outside the private 172.16 to 172.31 range.

questions.question: In what order does a DNS resolver contact servers to resolve a domain name?
questions.explanation: Root, TLD, Authoritative.

questions.question: How many usable hosts does each /28 subnet have?
questions.explanation: Host bits = 4, so 2^4 - 2 = 14.

questions.question: CSMA/CD is used in:
questions.explanation: CSMA/CD = wired Ethernet (Cable = Detection).

questions.question: A packet starts with a hop limit of 12 and passes through 4 routers before reaching the destination host. What is its remaining hop limit?
Which port does IMAP use?
questions.explanation: IMAP = 143.

questions.question: A 6000-bit packet passes through 2 intermediate routers using store-and-forward switching. Every link runs at 3 Mbps. Ignoring all other delays, what is the total delay?
questions.explanation: Per link 6000 / 3,000,000 = 2 ms. 3 links (N + 1), so 6 ms.

questions.question: Which type of switch port carries traffic for multiple VLANs over a single link?
questions.explanation: Trunk port carries multiple VLANs.

questions.question: Which switch feature lets a packet analyzer running in promiscuous mode inspect traffic from other ports?
questions.explanation: Port mirroring copies traffic to the analyzer's port.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a bit-oriented protocol?
questions.explanation: HDLC is bit-oriented.

questions.question: A /16 network is subnetted using a /19 mask. How many subnets are created?
Which protocol resolves an IP address to a MAC address?
questions.explanation: ARP: IP to MAC.

questions.question: A router receives a packet that is larger than the MTU of the outgoing link, and the DF bit is set. What does the router do?
options: Fragments the packet and forwards it
Drops the packet and sends an ICMP 'Fragmentation Needed' message
questions.explanation: DF set: drop and send ICMP 'Fragmentation Needed'.

questions.question: A PC can't reach a DHCP server. Which address range does it assign to itself?
What does the HTTP status code 301 mean?
questions.explanation: 301 = Moved Permanently (3xx = redirection).

questions.question: What is the IPv6 loopback address?
questions.explanation: ::1 is IPv6 loopback (127.0.0.1 is IPv4). :: is unspecified.

questions.question: A 2500-byte packet is sent on a 10 Mbps link. What is the transmission delay?
Which device separates broadcast domains?
questions.explanation: Router.

questions.question: In Selective Repeat ARQ, which frames are retransmitted after an error?
options: The lost frame and all frames after it
Only the frames before the lost one
questions.explanation: Selective Repeat resends only the lost frame.

questions.question: A telephone call, where both people can talk at the same time, is an example of which transmission mode?
questions.explanation: Both directions at the same time = full duplex.

questions.question: Which transport protocol does SMTP use?
questions.explanation: SMTP uses TCP.

questions.question: What is the size of an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: IPv6 = 128 bits; IPv4 = 32; MAC = 48.

questions.question: What is the network address of 192.168.4.150/26?
questions.explanation: /26 block = 64. 150 lies in 128 to 191, so network = .128.

questions.question: Which port does FTP use for its control connection?
questions.explanation: FTP control = 21.

questions.question: Which connector is used with coaxial cable?
questions.explanation: Coax = BNC.

questions.question: What is the size of the UDP header?
questions.explanation: UDP header = 8 bytes.

questions.question: Which type of address does IPv6 NOT have?
questions.explanation: No broadcast in IPv6.

questions.question: Which practice hides the IP addresses of backend servers?
questions.explanation: Reverse proxy protects/hides servers.

questions.question: In Go-Back-N ARQ, which frames are retransmitted when a frame is lost?
options: The lost frame and all frames sent after it
All frames since the connection started
questions.explanation: Go-Back-N goes back to the lost frame and resends everything after it.

questions.question: How many links are needed to fully connect 5 devices in a mesh topology?
How many networks are available in IPv4 Class B?
questions.explanation: 16 network bits minus 2 fixed bits (10) = 14, so 2¹⁴. 2¹⁶ is addresses per network.

questions.question: Each subnet must support 60 hosts. Which subnet mask should be used?
questions.explanation: Need 2^h - 2 >= 60, so h = 6 (62 hosts), prefix /26 = .192.

questions.question: The traceroute command discovers the path to a host by relying on:
options: Increasing TTL values and ICMP Time Exceeded messages
questions.explanation: Traceroute increments TTL and reads ICMP Time Exceeded replies.

questions.question: Which port does DNS use?
questions.explanation: DNS = 53.

questions.question: A link is 1000 km long and the signal speed is 2 × 10⁸ m/s. What is the propagation delay?
HTTP status codes in the 4xx range indicate:
questions.explanation: 4xx = client error; 5xx = server error.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for segmentation and reassembly?
questions.explanation: Transport layer.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)?
questions.explanation: STP prevents switching loops.

questions.question: Which PDU corresponds to the Data Link layer?
questions.explanation: Data Link PDU = Frame. 'Datagram' is UDP's unit.

questions.question: What is the broadcast address of the subnet containing 10.0.0.200/27?
questions.explanation: /27 block = 32. 200 lies in 192 to 223, so broadcast = .223.

questions.question: Which port does POP3 use?
What is the minimum size of an IPv4 header?
questions.explanation: IPv4 header = 20 bytes minimum, 60 maximum.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the DHCP messages?
questions.explanation: DORA.

questions.question: Which media access method do Wi-Fi networks use?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi = CSMA/CA.

questions.question: What is the total number of networks available in IPv4 Class B?
questions.explanation: 2¹⁴.

questions.question: Which function belongs to the Transport layer?
questions.explanation: Transport = segmentation and reassembly.

questions.question: A 1500-byte packet passes through 3 intermediate routers using store-and-forward switching. Every link runs at 12 Mbps. Ignoring all other delays, what is the total delay?
questions.explanation: 12000 bits / 12 Mbps = 1 ms per link; 4 links = 4 ms.

questions.question: Which of the following IP addresses is NOT private?
questions.explanation: 172.32 is outside 172.16 to 172.31, so it's public.

questions.question: Which protocol uses UDP port 69?
questions.explanation: TFTP (Trivial FTP) = UDP 69. No login or directory listing.

questions.question: NTP (Network Time Protocol) uses which port?
questions.explanation: NTP = UDP 123.

questions.question: LDAP uses which default port?
questions.explanation: LDAP = 389 (directory services such as Active Directory).

questions.question: Secure IMAP (IMAPS) uses which port?
questions.explanation: IMAPS = 993; POP3S = 995.

questions.question: Secure POP3 (POP3S) uses which port?
questions.explanation: POP3S = 995.

questions.question: Which port is commonly used for secure SMTP mail submission?
questions.explanation: Secure SMTP submission uses 587 (or 465). Plain SMTP = 25.

questions.question: SNMP traps are sent to which port?
questions.explanation: SNMP: 161 for queries, 162 for traps.

questions.question: The well-known port range is:
questions.explanation: Well-known 0–1023, registered 1024–49151, dynamic 49152–65535.

questions.question: A socket is identified by:
questions.explanation: Socket = IP address + port, e.g. 192.168.1.10:443.

questions.question: Which port does HTTP use by default?
questions.explanation: HTTP = 80; HTTPS = 443.

questions.question: SFTP transfers files securely by running over:
questions.explanation: SFTP runs over SSH (port 22). FTPS is FTP secured with SSL/TLS.

questions.question: FTPS is:
questions.explanation: FTPS = FTP + SSL/TLS. SFTP = file transfer over SSH.

questions.question: Which FTP transfer mode reduces data size during transmission to improve bandwidth efficiency?
questions.explanation: Compressed mode compresses the data. Stream is the default mode.

questions.question: HTTPS is:
options: A separate protocol unrelated to HTTP
questions.explanation: HTTPS = HTTP + TLS, on port 443.

questions.question: HTTP is described as stateless. This means:
options: The server doesn't remember previous requests, so cookies/sessions are used
questions.explanation: Stateless: each request is independent; cookies and sessions add state.

questions.question: Which HTTP method sends form data in the request body?
questions.explanation: POST sends data in the body; GET puts parameters in the URL.

questions.question: What does HTTP 401 indicate?
questions.explanation: 401 = not authenticated (log in). 403 = authenticated but not allowed.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code means 'Found' (temporary redirect)?
questions.explanation: 302 = Found (temporary). 301 = permanent.

questions.question: HTTP 304 means:
questions.explanation: 304 Not Modified: the client's cached copy is still valid.

questions.question: HTTP 503 means:
questions.explanation: 503 = Service Unavailable (server overloaded or down for maintenance).

questions.question: HTTP 201 means:
questions.explanation: 201 = Created, e.g. after a successful POST that creates a resource.

questions.question: Which DNS record maps a domain name to an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: AAAA = IPv6. A = IPv4.

questions.question: A CNAME record is used to:
options: Create an alias pointing one name to another
Map a name to an IPv4 address
questions.explanation: CNAME = canonical name (alias).

questions.question: Which DNS record is used for reverse lookup (IP to name)?
questions.explanation: PTR = pointer record, used for reverse DNS.

questions.question: DNS zone transfers between DNS servers use:
questions.explanation: Normal queries use UDP 53; zone transfers and large responses use TCP 53.

questions.question: In a recursive DNS query:
options: Each server only refers the client to another server
The root server returns the final IP
The client contacts the authoritative server directly
The resolver does all the work and returns the final answer
questions.explanation: Recursive: the resolver returns the final answer. Iterative: servers return referrals.

questions.question: Which protocol is best when the same mailbox must stay in sync on a phone and a laptop?
questions.explanation: IMAP keeps mail and folders on the server, so all devices stay in sync.

questions.question: MIME is used in email to:
questions.explanation: MIME extends email to carry attachments, images and non-ASCII text.

questions.question: WebDAV is:
options: An extension of HTTP for editing and managing files on a web server
questions.explanation: WebDAV extends HTTP for collaborative file editing on web servers.

questions.question: Telnet uses which port?
questions.explanation: Telnet = 23 (plaintext, insecure).

questions.question: A VPN primarily provides:
options: An encrypted tunnel over a public network
questions.explanation: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel across the internet.

questions.question: Which type of VPN connects two entire office networks?
questions.explanation: Site-to-site connects whole networks; remote-access connects one user.

questions.question: IPsec operates at which OSI layer?
questions.explanation: IPsec secures IP packets at the Network layer.

questions.question: A forward proxy acts on behalf of:
questions.explanation: A forward proxy acts for clients (filtering, caching, hiding client identity). A reverse proxy acts for servers.

questions.question: In a CDN, the servers located close to users are called:
questions.explanation: Edge servers cache content near users; the origin server holds the master copy.

questions.question: Compared with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, the 5 GHz band generally offers:
questions.explanation: 5 GHz = faster but shorter range; 2.4 GHz = longer range but slower.

questions.question: Bluetooth is defined under which IEEE standard and network type?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth = IEEE 802.15, a short-range Personal Area Network.

questions.question: How many steps does a normal TCP connection termination take?
questions.explanation: Termination is 4-way: FIN, ACK, FIN, ACK.

questions.question: A SYN flood attack exploits:
options: Half-open connections in the TCP 3-way handshake
questions.explanation: The attacker sends SYNs but never completes the handshake, exhausting server resources.

questions.question: ICMP is identified in the IPv4 Protocol field by which number?
questions.explanation: ICMP = 1, TCP = 6, UDP = 17. ICMP has no port numbers.

questions.question: Which value in the IPv4 Protocol field indicates UDP?
questions.explanation: UDP = 17.

questions.question: Static NAT provides:
options: A fixed one-to-one mapping between a private and a public IP
questions.explanation: Static NAT = fixed one-to-one; used for servers reachable from outside.

questions.question: In ARP, the request and the reply are sent as:
questions.explanation: ARP request is broadcast to the LAN; only the owner replies by unicast.

questions.question: The period for which a DHCP-assigned IP address is valid is called the:
questions.explanation: DHCP addresses are leased and must be renewed.

questions.question: OSPF is a:
options: Distance vector protocol using hop count
Link state protocol using Dijkstra's algorithm
Path vector protocol between autonomous systems
questions.explanation: OSPF = link state, Dijkstra (SPF). RIP = distance vector; BGP = path vector.

questions.question: Routes entered manually by an administrator are called:
questions.explanation: Static = manual; dynamic = learned automatically via routing protocols.

questions.question: What is the Ethernet MTU (maximum payload)?
questions.explanation: Ethernet MTU = 1500 bytes. A full frame is 64 to 1518 bytes.

questions.question: The first 24 bits of a MAC address are called the:
questions.explanation: OUI identifies the manufacturer; the last 24 bits identify the device.

questions.question: Which IEEE standard defines the Spanning Tree Protocol?
questions.explanation: 802.1D = STP; 802.1Q = VLAN tagging; 802.3ad = link aggregation.

questions.question: What is the minimum Ethernet frame size?
questions.explanation: Minimum 64 bytes, so collisions can be detected while the frame is still being sent.

questions.question: What is the maximum efficiency of Pure ALOHA?
questions.explanation: Pure ALOHA = 18.4%; Slotted ALOHA = 36.8%.

questions.question: The main advantage of a Hamming code over parity is that it can:
questions.explanation: Hamming codes locate and correct a single flipped bit; parity only detects.

questions.question: CIDR stands for:
questions.explanation: Classless Inter-Domain Routing: the /n prefix notation that replaced classful addressing.

questions.question: Combining 192.168.0.0/24, 192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24 and 192.168.3.0/24 into one route gives:
questions.explanation: Four /24s = 2 bits fewer, so /22. This is supernetting.

questions.question: Class D addresses (224–239) are used for:
questions.explanation: Class D = multicast; Class E = experimental.

questions.question: Which IPv4 address is used for loopback?
questions.explanation: 127.0.0.1 = loopback (this machine).

questions.question: How many usable hosts are available on a /30 subnet?
questions.explanation: 2^2 - 2 = 2; used for point-to-point router links.

questions.question: 'Slow start' is part of which TCP mechanism?
questions.explanation: Slow start belongs to congestion control (protects the network).
